page.layout: One printed page, single column of running text, full width. Running head at the top right. No marginal notes. Faint fragments of the next lines at the bottom edge.

main_text.p: Tum [illegible, ~8 letters] varii, muneribus inter se differentes, e ditioribus singularum tribuum a tribulibus quoque designati ad munera quaedam suarum tribuum nomine suis sumptibus obeunda, ut [illegible, ~9 letters] multiplices, qui choros ludionum ludosque; varios, actiones scenicas, saltatores, cantores, psaltas in theatris exhibebant, item [illegible, ~9 letters], [illegible, ~9 letters] [?], quos choragos, exercitationum praefides, epulones, triremium magistros, collatores latine dixeris: omnes fere juvenes, hoc honore onerofo aditu sibi ad honores alios aperientes. Praeterea in magistratuum ordine fuere [illegible, ~10 letters] mundi muliebris curam agentes, ne is modum excederet, & mulieres parum modestas multa corripientes: item [illegible, ~8 letters] ac [illegible, ~8 letters], quorum munus erat, convivia & conviviorum sumptus, & convivarum numerum inspicere, & curare, ne quid contra leges committeretur. De praefectis coloniarum deducendarum dubites, an magistratibus eos accenseas. In numerum quidem ordinariorum venire non poterant. Nam nec quotannis, sed pro re nata, creabantur, nec annuum imperium, sed quamdiu res poscebat, tenebant. Munus tamen illustre fuit cum[illegible, ~3 letters]

page.notes: Greek words are only partly legible in the scan and were not guessed; the first Greek word, the three Greek titles after "item" and the Greek words after "fuere", "item" and "ac" are marked illegible. The word at the bottom edge is cut off by the page edge. Faint fragments at the bottom (tc-, ςς-, numbers) look like signature or catchword remnants of the next page and are not transcribed, since they cannot be read with confidence.
